comments: Canoe-body force coefficients for sail::HullForceModule. The keel and rudder are separate foil modules and are not counted here. Hull dimensions (lwl, tc, lcb_x_canoe, sinkage_m) come from hull_hydro.json conditions.sailing.result and the water density from hull_resistance.json water, so the absolute values below follow the hull. Velocities are water-relative at the centre of lateral resistance (CLR), including the yaw-rate part of the point velocity but not the roll- and pitch-rate parts, whose damping belongs to damping.json. Resistance: the hull_resistance.json model at the axial speed |u_ax| (horizontal velocity along the horizontal heading), directed opposite the horizontal velocity; the cross-flow part of the velocity is resisted by the sway terms below instead. Side force: R. T. Jones low-aspect-ratio wing theory (NACA Report 835, 1946), C_L = pi*AR*alpha/2, i.e. L = q*(pi/2)*b^2*alpha independent of planform area, applied to the canoe body mirrored in a rigid free surface (span b = 2*Tc) and halved: L = 0.5*rho*pi*Tc^2*U^2*beta. It is written as L = k*u_ax*u_lat with k = slope_multiplier*0.5*rho*pi*Tc^2, which equals the linear law at small leeway, vanishes at beam-on drift, and is symmetric for inflow from astern. Jones's induced drag is L*alpha/2. Munk correction: the integrator applies the ideal-fluid Munk yaw moment -(A_sway - A_surge)*u*v from the constant added mass; this module adds +fraction*(A_sway - A_surge)*u*v, with u and v the body-frame CG velocity the integrator itself uses (no current, no yaw-rate arm), so that exactly the fraction cancels, and A from the mass model, faded in like the side force, because the lifting canoe body carries only part of the ideal-fluid moment. Sway and yaw damping: generalised force -(b_lin*q + b_quad*|q|*q), as in damping.json, with q the horizontal lateral velocity at the CLR for sway (applied along the horizontal 90 degrees to port of the heading, so that a heeled hull's heave velocity is not damped again) and the body-frame yaw rate for yaw. Sway and yaw have no hydrostatic stiffness, so they cannot be given as fractions of critical damping; instead b_quad is cross-flow drag (Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag, 1965, ch. 3) over a lateral profile whose draft is Tc*(1 - (2x/Lwl)^2): sway b_quad = 0.5*rho*C_D*A_lat with A_lat = (2/3)*Lwl*Tc, yaw b_quad = 0.5*rho*C_D*Tc*Lwl^4/96 (the strip integral of |x|^3 over that profile, about mid-Lwl). b_lin = b_quad * crossover speed for sway and b_quad * crossover speed / (Lwl/2) for yaw, so below the crossover the damping is linear.

depth_fraction_of_tc.source: elliptic spanwise loading on the canoe body mirrored in the free surface
depth_fraction_of_tc.method: the CLR is at hull-frame x = lcb_x_canoe and z = sinkage_m - depth_fraction_of_tc*tc, i.e. on the sailing flotation plane less this fraction of the canoe draft; 4/(3*pi) = 0.424 is the centroid of a half-elliptic load from the root, and the parabolic draft profile's lateral-area centroid (0.40) is close to it

slope_multiplier.source: R. T. Jones, Properties of low-aspect-ratio pointed wings at speeds below and above the speed of sound, NACA Report 835 (1946)
slope_multiplier.method: multiplies Jones's lift slope; 1.0 takes the slender-wing value unchanged. The canoe body's aspect ratio is about 0.1, where Jones is the right limit, but the free surface is not a rigid wall at speed and heel changes the immersed profile, neither of which is modelled

induced_drag_factor.method: induced drag = factor * |L| * |sin(beta)|, Jones's D_i = L*alpha/2 at small angle

blend_speed.method: side force and induced drag are multiplied by smoothstep(U/blend_speed), so the leeway angle, undefined at rest, never sets a force direction below this speed

crossflow_drag_coefficient.source: estimate from Hoerner, Fluid-Dynamic Drag (1965), ch. 3, cross-flow drag of elongated bodies, and ch. 10 for flat-bottomed ship sections
crossflow_drag_coefficient.method: the mirrored J/80 section is an ellipse of half-width 0.96 m by half-height 0.28 m moving along its long axis, a bluff-to-streamlined shape whose drag on its height lies well below a flat plate's 2; 0.5 on the lateral area is a mid estimate, with the keel and rudder carrying most of the boat's lateral damping in their own modules

linear_crossover_speed.method: b_lin = b_quad * crossover speed: the speed below which skin friction and wave radiation, roughly linear, exceed the cross-flow drag

fraction.source: Clarke, Gedling and Hine (1983), The application of manoeuvring criteria in hull design using linear theory, Trans. RINA 125: N'v = -pi*(T/L)^2*(0.5 + 2.4*T/L), about half the full Munk value
fraction.method: slender-body Kutta condition cancels the after-body half of the ideal-fluid Munk moment

crossflow_drag_coefficient.method: the sway cross-flow coefficient applied strip by strip to the lateral velocity x*r

linear_crossover_speed.method: lateral speed at the waterline ends, r*Lwl/2, below which yaw damping is linear; b_lin = b_quad * crossover speed / (Lwl/2)
